  IAPWE Professional Development Series 3 Introduction  If your web content isn't attracting prospects and furthering your business goals (sign-ups, trials, sales etc.), it's not doing its job. Consistently creating relevant, fresh, and searchable content is critical to your website's success. However, simply updating your blog isn't enough. Your content must perform on many levels.  Effective web content needs to:               Effective Web ContentIncrease AwarenessEngage Your TargetForge a ConnectionGenerate and Convert LeadsBoost Search Engine Rank

PAGE_4:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 4 Ø Increase awareness of your brand Ø Engage your target Ø Forge a connection with your audience Ø Generate and convert more quality leads Ø Boost search engine ranking  You might find that after the initial rush of a website launch, visits start to fall. Or, after years of website success, numbers are trending downward and it's not clear why. You have fewer page visits, and the visitors that you do have are spending less time on the site. If this is the case, your web content, and the way your website is structured, could be the culprit.   Developing a business website isn't a one-time event. It’s an ongoing process of testing, tweaking, and anticipating what your audience wants. Your site should evolve with your business, your industry, and current trends. This doesn’t mean that your website needs a complete overhaul (although you can definitely do this if you think it's necessary). Instead, if you apply even two or three of the web content and keyword strategies in this course, you’ll take a big leap forward in achieving some of your business goals. The course will also help keep visitors on your site with some small, but important, modifications to your website's structure.  If you have an active business website, understand the fundamentals of creating website content, and are now ready to take it to the next level – this course will help you get there.

PAGE_5:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 5 The Evolution of Web Content  Your web content should not only communicate the most important features of your business, it should also attract and appeal to people who are looking for what you're selling. It is critical to understand who your audience is and how they find you. In addition to your web marketing strategy (developing strong social media presence, participation in forums, visibility on review sites, and more), search engines also act as a matchmaker between you and your audience. But the way search engines have connected people to websites has changed over the years, so your content must change and adapt along with it. In the past, people added keywords, backlinks, and other elements to their websites to increase their search engine page rank. The more relevant keywords they had, the higher they would rank. They would often supplement their SEO strategy with targeted ads. While this is still part of an effective web strategy, it is becoming increasingly difficult to get the desired results.  Search engines started to notice that many highly optimized sites weren't providing real value to visitors. Pages were being stacked with keywords, but the actual content on the pages had little relevance to the search. Search engines, such as Google, started changing and evolving their algorithms to provide higher quality results for their users.  This means that small businesses have needed to adapt their content, SEO strategy, and website structure to continue showing up in search engine results. This course will introduce you to many of these innovations and trends. This course will also show you how to create content that appeals to your target audience and keep them engaged.

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 6 Here is your roadmap through the course:           Learning Objectives: By the time you complete this course, you'll be able to: Ø Evaluate and analyze your target audience and conduct a website content review, giving you a clear picture of where you are, and where you need to be. Ø Identify where you need to update the structure of your website and how essential pages are presented, so you can increase visitor engagement and keep them on your site. Ø Recognize the importance of long-form content and pick tangible ways to incorporate it into your site. Ø Apply long-form content strategies (Pillar, Skyscraper, and Ladder) to increase site visits and boost search engine ranking.   IAPWE Professional Development Series 7 Ø Use online tools and audience feedback to generate new content ideas, including short-form content that will grab attention and engage new visitors. Ø Identify ways to incorporate different content series (Welcome, Buzz-Building) into your overall web content strategy. Ø Consolidate and implement your learning and plan future action steps, so that you can achieve the goals you set for this course and develop further.  This course is delivered in 7 modules, taking you step by step through the process of evolving your web content, with the ultimate goal of getting more visitors to your site and increasing sales. Each module builds on the previous module, so while you can skip around if you prefer, it's recommended that you work through the course in the presented order.  As you progress through this course, use the Action Guide to help you complete the Actions Steps at the end of each module.   Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it. In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain.  Now that you're clear about what you want this course to deliver, we are ready to get started!

  IAPWE Professional Development Series 8 Module 1 – Laying the Foundation: Evaluate Your Target Audience & Content  Before you dive into the website content strategies in this course, it is a valuable exercise to take stock of where your site currently stands. The two most important elements to review are:      1. Your target audience 2. Your existing content   Later in this course, you’ll explore different web content strategies to attract more visitors, but if your content doesn't resonate with your target audience or current customer base, your hard work will not produce the desired results. Also keep in mind that as you start to adopt some of these web content strategies, you will need to work with your existing content.    Your target audienceYour existing content

PAGE_9:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 9 Understand Your Target Audience  The key to powerful content is understanding your audience. What do they like, what do they need, and what do they expect when they visit your site? It is always a good idea to periodically reexamine current followers, customers, and potential customers to get an understanding of your actual audience versus your anticipated audience, or your audience from one, two, or five years ago.  For example, you may have expected your product or service to appeal to a younger age group, but the majority of your follows, inquiries, or sales now come from an older crowd. If there has been a shift, you will need to adapt your content to appeal to your evolving audience. Take this time to analyze your audience, focusing on the following areas:        Ø Demographics Ø Psychographics  Ø Purchasing Behavior DemographicsPsychographicsPurchasing Behavior

PAGE_10:
NEXT LEVEL WEBSITE CONTENT 
  IAPWE Professional Development Series 10 Demographics Demographics include unemotional, fact-based information about your audience, including: Ø Age Ø Geographic location Ø Education level Ø Marital status Ø Occupation  You can find some of this information through Google Analytics. You can also ask your audience for it directly. For example, if they sign up for a free eBook, in addition to their email address, ask them to provide one or two pieces of demographic information.   Psychographics Psychographics explore the emotional and personal information about your audience, including:  Ø Needs and desires Ø Values Ø Hobbies Ø Goals Ø Pain points (areas where they're struggling)
